questions.question: Wernicke encephalopathy is an acute clinical syndrome of ataxia, confusion, and oculomotor dysfunction caused by a deficiency in which vitamin?
questions.detail: This deficiency is most common in patients with alcohol use disorder or secondary malnutrition, such as from hyperemesis or bariatric surgery.

questions.question: Which combination of brain structures is most frequently affected by symmetric hyperintensity on FLAIR in Wernicke encephalopathy?
choices: Medial thalami, mammillary bodies, and periaqueductal gray matter
Splenium of the corpus callosum and dentate nuclei
questions.detail: Affected areas typically demonstrate symmetric hyperintensity on FLAIR and restricted diffusion, with contrast enhancement seen in up to 50% of cases.

questions.question: In chronic hepatic encephalopathy, symmetric hyperintensity on noncontrast T1-weighted images within the globi pallidi and substantia nigrae is thought to be due to the accumulation of:
questions.detail: This finding is a reversible clinical syndrome often seen in patients with chronic liver disease and portal hypertension.

questions.question: Acute hyperammonemic encephalopathy, seen in acute liver failure, characteristically involves symmetric restricted diffusion and FLAIR hyperintensity in the:
choices: Putamina with sparing of the globi pallidi
questions.detail: This pattern typically features relative sparing of the occipital lobes and perirolandic region.

questions.question: The 'lentiform fork sign' (FLAIR hyperintensity outlining the putamina) is an imaging finding associated with metabolic acidosis in the setting of:
questions.detail: Uremic encephalopathy occurs in renal failure; the 'lentiform fork sign' characteristically outlines the lateral and medial boundaries of the putamina.

questions.question: Selective hemorrhagic necrosis of the putamina with relative sparing of the globi pallidi is the hallmark imaging feature of:
questions.detail: Methanol poisoning causes severe metabolic acidosis and can lead to rapid progression to a comatose state.

questions.question: In contrast to methanol poisoning, carbon monoxide poisoning characteristically results in bilateral symmetric necrosis of the:
questions.detail: This appears as hyperintensity with a hypointense rim on FLAIR and restricted diffusion on DWI.

questions.question: Osmotic demyelination (central pontine myelinolysis) typically occurs following the aggressive correction of:
questions.detail: Rapid osmotic changes cause endothelial damage and myelin-damaging toxin release; extrapontine sites like the thalami or basal ganglia are involved in up to 50% of cases.

questions.question: Marchiafava-Bignami disease is a rare disorder primarily associated with chronic alcohol use and is characterized by demyelination and necrosis of the:
questions.detail: Imaging shows T2 prolongation and restricted diffusion within the corpus callosum, often extending into the pericallosal white matter.

questions.question: Symmetric hyperintensity on FLAIR involving the cerebellar dentate nuclei and the splenium of the corpus callosum is highly characteristic of toxicity from which drug?
questions.detail: While more common with prolonged treatment, it has been described with short courses; patients typically present with cerebellar dysfunction.

questions.question: Which imaging pattern is most characteristic of methotrexate-induced brain toxicity?
choices: Symmetric hyperintensity of the medial thalami
Bilateral, asymmetric white matter lesions crossing vascular territories with sparing of subcortical U-fibers
Diffuse cortical ribboning with sparing of the motor cortex
Coarse bilateral calcification of the basal ganglia
Symmetric hyperintensity of the globi pallidi on T1
questions.detail: These lesions show diffusion restriction; unlike malignancy, the pattern and enhancement typically disappear without treatment.

questions.question: Fahr disease is an important differential diagnosis for parathyroid dysfunction because it also presents with bilateral basal ganglia calcification, but it is distinguished by:
choices: Presence of the lentiform fork sign
Restricted diffusion in the dentate nuclei
questions.detail: Fahr disease is idiopathic or genetic and lacks the laboratory abnormalities associated with parathyroid dysfunction.

questions.question: In the setting of parathyroid dysfunction or Fahr disease, how does coarse basal ganglia calcification typically appear on T1-weighted MRI?
questions.detail: Minerals like dispersed calcium can cause T1 shortening, resulting in hyperintensity.

questions.question: Elevated NAA (N-acetylaspartate) on MR spectroscopy is a characteristic finding in which metabolic leukodystrophy?
questions.detail: While most abnormalities cause decreased NAA, it is characteristically elevated in Canavan disease.

questions.question: On MR spectroscopy, an elevated lactate peak is a clue for mitochondrial encephalopathies such as:
questions.detail: Lactate reflects anaerobic glycolysis and abnormal tissue damage, serving as a clue for conditions like Leigh syndrome.
